questions.explain: QUEUE_DELAY of 0 means synchronous writes (transaction cannot commit until the audit record is written); 1000ms allows asynchronous buffering for high-throughput environments.

questions.explain: ON_FAILURE=FAIL_OPERATION rolls back only the audited operations when the audit target is unavailable, whereas CONTINUE keeps the server running and SHUTDOWN stops it.
questions.q: Which ON_FAILURE option rolls back only the audited operations when the audit target becomes unavailable?

questions.explain: sys.fn_get_audit_file is a table-valued function that reads binary audit files as rows, so you can filter, aggregate, and join audit data with plain T-SQL.
questions.q: Which function reads SQL Server audit files so you can query audit records with T-SQL?

questions.explain: Monitoring AUDIT_CHANGE_GROUP detects audit configuration changes (AUSC = Audit Session Change), closing the loop on audit tampering at the configuration level.
